method: Same 16 permission cases through each adapter and shared current validation. Required constraints scored; extras reported, not all penalized. Facts: same 24 texts, four binary labels each. Serial calls; chat timeout 15s and one SDK retry for both. Retries included. Jev fact requests capped at 1s. No payment API calls. Rule-verification controls and replay are a separate supplemental run. Fact target scores are annotated from unchanged raw predictions; original strict all-flag scores are retained.

limitations: Authored diagnostics, not independently labeled production data. Two repeats do not create independent cases.
Rule pass requires the labeled constraints, intent and forbidden-field checks; extra rules are recorded but not all counted as errors.

Fact target score uses the one behavior each case was authored to probe. Strict all-flag match additionally treats every omitted label as false; subscription/add-on overlap makes some of those cross-label errors ambiguous.
Application adapters are compared, including their prompts and shared current validation; this is not an identical-prompt model leaderboard.
Apertus used its configured service and existing prompt. All requests used synthetic data. No payment or permission activation API was called.
One-second fact-reader fallback did not activate in this run. That does not establish production availability.
45-purchase replay measures agreement and monotonic safety only: the pack has no ground-truth payment decisions.
Jev rule verification is shadow-only by default: enforce mode rejected valid rules at threshold 0.9. Thresholds were not tuned on these results.
